hero.title: The questions we actually get asked.
hero.answer: HARGILE is an independent web studio in Brussels, building custom web applications for SMEs. Here are direct answers to the questions asked before choosing an agency: how much a custom application costs in Belgium, how long it takes, agency or freelancer, and who owns the code at the end. Missing yours? Write to us.

items.q: How do you choose a web agency in Brussels to build a custom application?
items.a: Three things can be checked before you sign. Who actually writes the code: at HARGILE, design and development are done in-house in Brussels, never subcontracted. How the price is set: during scoping, before the project starts, and it does not move afterwards. And who owns the code at the end: you do. The rest — references, availability, working language — fits in one call.

items.q: How does a custom web development project unfold, from scoping to launch?
items.a: Always in the same order: a scoping phase where we define scope, priorities and price together; the design of flows and screens; development, with regular check-ins; testing; launch. Everything is done in-house by the same team, and you have one direct contact from start to finish.

items.q: How long does it take to build a custom web application for an SME?
items.a: It depends on the scope — and the scope is fixed during scoping, not discovered along the way. The most concrete benchmark: our MVP offer delivers a complete, usable product in 30 days. A showcase site can be faster; a richer business application takes several months, in planned stages.

items.q: Is it really possible to build an MVP in 30 days?
items.a: Yes, on one condition: the scope is frozen before we start. Week 1, scoping and design; weeks 2 and 3, development; week 4, testing and launch. What comes out is a real product, live, usable by real users — not a mockup. Anything that does not fit inside the 30 days is priced separately, and comes after.

items.q: What should you prepare before contacting a web agency about a custom project?
items.a: Nothing is required: your idea and your business reality are enough. Examples of sites you like, known constraints or an existing system to take over all help — but turning all that into a clear scope is exactly what the scoping phase is for.

items.q: Where is HARGILE based, and do you work with SMEs across Belgium?
items.a: In Brussels. We work with SMEs all over Belgium: on site when meeting in person actually serves the project, remotely the rest of the time — being close is a matter of availability, not kilometres. Our two working languages are French and English, and multilingual sites are routine: La Marquisette is trilingual, this one exists in French and English.

items.q: How much does it cost to build a custom web application for an SME in Belgium?
items.a: There is no honest one-size-fits-all rate: the price depends on the scope. Our commitment is about the method: the price is set during scoping, announced before the project starts, and it does not move — no time-based billing, no surprise overruns. For a first product, the 30-day MVP offer comes at a fixed price.

items.q: Can you get a fixed price for custom development, with no time-based billing?
items.a: Yes — and it works because the scope is frozen before we start: scoping defines precisely what will be delivered, and the price matches that scope. If a new idea appears mid-project, it is priced separately and you decide whether to add it — the initial price does not change.

items.q: Should an SME hire a web agency or a freelance developer?
items.a: A freelancer is often the right call for a well-scoped job that needs a single skill. A team becomes useful when design, development and deployment move in parallel, and when someone still has to be there in two years. HARGILE is an independent studio: one direct contact like a freelancer, a team behind it to ship and maintain.

items.q: Who owns the source code at the end of a web development project?
items.a: You do. Code and data are yours on delivery: you can host elsewhere, hand the next step to another team, or keep going with us. You stay by choice, never out of necessity.

items.q: Which technologies do you use to build a custom web application?
items.a: Modern, proven web technologies — notably React and Next.js: this very site is built with that framework. The precise choice is made during scoping, based on your project and your existing systems — never the other way around.

items.q: Should an SME choose WordPress or custom development for its website?
items.a: WordPress makes sense for publishing content on a tight budget. Custom becomes the right choice when your site has to do something: booking, selling, business processes — or when a generic theme holds your image back. Ecole du Bonheur came with a generic WordPress; we turned it into a digital experience worthy of its project.

items.q: Who maintains a website after it goes live?
items.a: We do, if you want us to — the site is not left on its own: we maintain what we ship, updates, security and evolutions. Maintenance is offered separately, with no obligation: since you own the code, you remain free to entrust it to whomever you want.

items.q: Is SEO included in a web development project?
items.a: The foundations, yes, always: clean structure, speed, structured data, machine-readable content — everything that makes a site able to rank well. The ongoing visibility work (content, rank tracking, AI citations) is what our dedicated SEO offer is for.

items.q: When does integrating AI actually make sense in an SME's web project?
items.a: When it changes the outcome: automating repetitive tasks, smart search, making your data work. And when it adds nothing to your case, we tell you — an AI integration must justify itself with a measurable result, not with a trend.

hero.title: AI where it changes the outcome.
hero.answer: We integrate artificial intelligence into SME products and processes — only where it delivers a measurable result: fewer repetitive tasks, better service, data finally put to work. When AI adds nothing to your case, we tell you.

useCases.title: Four places where AI earns its place.

automation.title: Back-office automation
automation.signal: Your team copies data from one tool to another.
automation.outcome: Hours recovered every week, and fewer input errors.

content.title: Content & visibility
content.signal: You know what to say, but never have time to publish it.
content.outcome: A regular presence, fed by your real expertise.

support.title: Customer support
support.signal: The same questions keep coming, and the answers keep waiting.
support.outcome: Instant answers to common questions, and a team focused on the cases that matter.

data.title: Making your data work
data.signal: The numbers exist, but nobody looks at them.
data.outcome: Decisions backed by your data, not by gut feeling.

honesty.title: And when AI is not the answer?
honesty.text: We say so. An AI integration is only worth it if it changes a result that matters to you — not because of a trend. If a simple script, a better process or nothing at all does the job, that is what we will recommend. That, too, is what a technical partner is for.

flow.title: Decided before the first line of code
flow.text: Which data leaves your systems, to which provider, under which contract: that is settled during scoping, before any integration. Nothing gets wired blindly into an API because it happens to be convenient.

sensitive.title: What is sensitive stays with you
sensitive.text: When data is sensitive, we favour solutions that keep it on your own infrastructure. GDPR is not a box ticked at the end of a project: it decides the architecture.

reversible.title: Reversible by design
reversible.text: The AI provider stays replaceable — models move too fast to lock yourself into one. And the code that calls them belongs to you, like the rest.

items.q: Where does our data go?
items.a: That is defined before anything is integrated: which data leaves your company, to which provider, under which contract. When data is sensitive, we favour solutions that keep it with you. Nothing gets plugged in without you knowing exactly what flows where.

items.q: Do we need a big budget to start?
items.a: No. We start with the use case that has the best result-to-effort ratio — often a targeted automation — and we measure before expanding. AI is rolled out in steps, not in a big bang.

items.q: Will we be locked into an AI provider?
items.a: We design the integration so the provider stays replaceable: models evolve fast, and your product should not be married to one of them. And as with everything we ship, the code belongs to you.

items.q: Where do we start if we have never used AI?
items.a: With a conversation about your processes, not about technology. Together we identify one measurable task where AI can make a difference, we put it in place, and we judge it on the result.

hero.title: From idea to product, in 30 days.
hero.answer: Yes, a real product can launch in one month. Our MVP offer turns your idea into a usable product in 30 days, at a fixed price announced before we start: week 1, scope and design; weeks 2 and 3, development; week 4, tests and launch.

w1.label: Week 1
w1.title: Scope & design
w1.text: Together we define the scope: what belongs in the MVP, and what waits for v2. Mockups and user flows are approved before a single line of code is written.

w23.label: Weeks 2–3
w23.title: Development
w23.text: We build the product with modern web technologies. You follow progress continuously — no three-week tunnel without news.
deliverables: Working product by the end of week 3

w4.label: Week 4
w4.title: Test & launch
w4.text: We test, fix and polish — then go live. Your MVP is in its first users' hands by day 30.

included.title: What's included — and what isn't.
in: Ownership of the code and the data
out: The business content only you can write
Long-term maintenance — offered separately, with no obligation

price.title: Fixed price, no surprises.
price.text: The price is announced before the project starts, and it does not move: no time-based billing, no overrun discovered along the way. If a new idea comes up mid-project, it is priced separately and you decide.

scope.title: The boundary that holds the promise.
scope.text: Thirty days is not a question of speed: it is a question of scope. Week 1 exists to cut — to keep the smallest version that already gives real users something, and to set the rest aside without losing it.
points: What overflows goes onto the v2 roadmap: prioritised and written down, not forgotten.
The business content stays yours: copy, photos, prices — nobody else can write those for you.
The one real condition on our side of the deadline: someone who can decide, available in week 1 and able to settle questions quickly at each checkpoint.

proofCase.text: La Marquisette: a character cottage in the Belgian Ardennes, launched with a tight scope — a trilingual showcase site with integrated booking.

items.q: What happens after the 30 days?
items.a: The product is yours and it is live. From there, three paths: you continue on your own (you own the code), we iterate together towards v2, or we handle maintenance. Nothing is imposed — you stay by choice.

items.q: What do I need to provide to keep the deadline?
items.a: Your availability in week 1 for scoping decisions, then quick feedback at each check-in. The 30-day deadline assumes a reachable decision-maker — that is the only real condition.

items.q: What if my idea is too big for 30 days?
items.a: That is what week 1 is for: cutting it down. An MVP is not your full product — it is the smallest version that delivers value to real users. Whatever does not fit goes on the v2 roadmap — not forgotten, prioritised.

items.q: Is the MVP a real product or a throwaway prototype?
items.a: A real product, built on foundations made to last — the same care as our long-term projects. If the MVP validates your market, v2 is built on top of it, not from scratch.

hero.title: Your visibility, automated.
hero.answer: We make SMEs visible where their customers actually search: on Google, and now in the answers of AI assistants like ChatGPT and Perplexity. Technical SEO, content and measurement — automated where possible, for a durable result rather than a one-off campaign.

audit.title: Audit
audit.text: First, the facts: what makes you visible today, what holds you back, and where the queries that matter to your business are.

tech.title: Technical
tech.text: A site engines can read without obstacles: speed, structure, structured data, content present from the first load.

content.title: Content
content.text: Pages that each answer one real customer question — the format Google and answer engines cite.

measure.title: Measure
measure.text: Rankings, traffic, AI citations: we track what changes, and we adjust. What is not measured does not improve.

metaProof.title: This page is the demonstration.
metaProof.text: The method we propose is the one we apply to our own site:
points: All the content is in the HTML from the first response — readable by search engines and AI assistants alike.
Every page carries its structured data (schema.org), validated automatically before every release.
Every page exists in French and English, with the tags that tell engines which one to serve.
View this page's source: it is all there.

measured.title: This page, in numbers.
measured.lead: Measured on {date} on this very page, with {tool}, under mobile conditions. You can run the tool yourself and land on the same figures — that is the whole point of publishing them.
measured.note: The main content paint is still over its 2.5 second threshold, and we leave it on display rather than picking the numbers that suit us. That one is work in progress. An agency that only publishes its good scores is not telling you what it measures: it is telling you what it shows.

geo.title: Being cited by AI answers.
geo.lead: When a client asks ChatGPT or Perplexity which agency builds web applications in Brussels, the assistant answers by citing its sources. Being one of those sources is where visibility now starts — and it is worked page by page.

readable.title: Content machines can read
readable.text: The answers are in the HTML on the first response, with no JavaScript to run. An answer engine that only sees an empty page will never cite anything.

structured.title: Structured data
structured.text: Every page states what it is and who wrote it, in schema.org format. That is what lets an engine attach an answer to one specific company.

answers.title: One page, one real question
answers.text: Pages are written to answer, plainly, a question your clients actually ask. That is the format answer engines quote and attribute.

closing.title: What this does not guarantee.
closing.text: Nobody controls the models, and nobody can promise you will be cited. What we commit to is the method, and transparency about what it produces.

measures.title: What we measure — and what we don't promise.
measures.text: You don't have to take our word for it. The numbers are tracked and shared: we look at the same ones you do, at the same time.
points: Positions on the queries that matter to your business, not the ones that look good in a report.
Organic traffic, with the honest timeline: a few weeks for what is technical, several months for what is editorial.
Pages cited by answer engines, tracked on the same footing as Google positions.
measures.refusal: What we will not sell: a guaranteed first position. Nobody serious can promise it, and an agency that does has already told you something about the rest.

proofCase.text: VENIZI sells its jewellery online and across a network of 50 boutiques in Belgium and France — a catalogue where every product has to be findable.

items.q: How long before we see results?
items.a: SEO is a long-term investment: technical fixes show effects within weeks, content within months. It is slower than advertising — but it does not stop when the budget does.

items.q: Do you guarantee the first position on Google?
items.a: No — and nobody serious can: results depend on an algorithm nobody controls. What we do guarantee is the method — clean technical foundations, content that answers real questions, measurement — and transparency about what it produces.

items.q: What does being visible in AI answers mean?
items.a: When someone asks ChatGPT or Perplexity which agency can build a web application in Brussels, those assistants cite their sources. Being cited is the new ranking — and it can be worked on: machine-readable content, structured data, and clear answers to the questions people actually ask.

items.q: How do we track results?
items.a: You do not have to take our word for it: rankings, organic traffic and cited pages are tracked and shared. We look at the same numbers you do.

hero.title: Custom web applications for SMEs.
hero.answer: We design, build and maintain custom web applications entirely in-house, from Brussels. No outsourcing: the team that designs your product is the one that codes it and keeps it alive. And on delivery, the code and the data belong to you.

madeInHouse.title: Everything happens in-house.
madeInHouse.lead: Designed, built and maintained by the same team, in Brussels. Here is what that adds up to: every square is a site that is live today — click one, you are there.

grid.hint: Newest first. Click a square to open the site.

ownership.title: Your code, your data.
ownership.text: On delivery you own the code and your data. You can leave, host elsewhere, or keep going with us — by choice.

deliverables.title: What you receive.
deliverables.lead: At the end of a project, four things are yours. Nothing stays with us: everything is designed and built in-house in Brussels, never subcontracted, and what comes out of it leaves with you.

design.text: Screens and user journeys, drawn by the same team that then codes them. You get the mockups, not only the result on screen.

code.titleRest: in a repository under your name
code.text: All of the code, in a repository you own. Another team can pick it up without having to ask us for anything.

live.text: Deployed on your own domain, in one language or several — a trilingual site is a routine request here, not an exotic add-on.

keys.text: Hosting, domain, analytics: the accounts are in your name and handed over to you. You stay with us by choice, never because the door is shut.

priceMethod.title: How the price is set.
priceMethod.text: There is no honest single rate for a custom application: the price depends on what there is to build. What we commit to is the method — the price is settled during scoping, announced before development starts, and does not move afterwards.
points: The scope is frozen during scoping: the price matches that scope, in writing.
No billing by time spent, so no overrun discovered along the way.
An idea that comes up mid-project is quoted separately: you decide whether to take it or keep it for later, and the initial price does not change.
priceMethod.note: For a first product, the MVP in 30 days offer applies the same method, with a fixed price and a launch date both known from the start.

design.text: The design starts from your business, not from a template. Mockups and user flows are drawn in-house, with you.

build.text: Developed with modern web technologies — like this site. No plugin assembly: code we know line by line.

maintain.text: After launch, the foundations keep being cared for. You stay by choice, never out of necessity.

cases.title: Three proofs rather than a promise.

edb.text: A generic WordPress rebuilt into a digital experience worthy of a school that deserved better.

marquisette.text: A 19th-century cottage in the heart of the Belgian Ardennes — a trilingual showcase site with integrated booking.

venizi.text: Venetian-inspired jewellery, sold online and across a network of 50 boutiques in Belgium and France.

items.q: Do you take over an existing site or application?
items.a: Yes. A good share of our projects are rebuilds or takeovers: we audit what exists, keep what holds, and rebuild what blocks you. Ecole du Bonheur arrived with a generic WordPress; it left with a site worthy of its educational project.

items.q: Can you build a multilingual site?
items.a: Yes — in Belgium it is almost a habit. La Marquisette is a trilingual site with integrated booking, and this very site is served in French and English with search optimisation for each language.

items.q: Do you do the design too?
items.a: Yes. Design and development are done by the same team, in-house. You do not have to coordinate a design agency and a developer: mockups, user flows and code come from the same place.

items.q: Do you build e-commerce?
items.a: Yes. VENIZI sells its jewellery online and across a network of 50 boutiques in Belgium and France. Online store, payment, catalogue: we build what your sales actually need.

hero.title: What we deliver.
hero.answer: HARGILE is an independent web studio based in Brussels. We design, build and maintain custom web applications for SMEs, integrate AI where it changes the outcome, automate your search visibility, and turn an idea into a live MVP in 30 days, at a fixed price.

deliverables: An honest no when it adds nothing

spine.text: Every offer is a delivery commitment, not a catalogue line. You talk to the team that designs it and writes the code, from scoping to launch.
